title: Evaluation of the Quran Reading Completion Program at SD Negeri 025 Central Balikpapan: A Goal-Oriented Evaluation Model
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the Quran Reading Completion Program (Tuntas Baca Quran/TBQ) at SD Negeri 025 Balikpapan Tengah using Ralph W. Tyler’s Goal-Oriented Evaluation model. The TBQ program was implemented to improve students’ ability to read the Quran accurately, fluently, and in accordance with the rules of tajwid. This study employed a qualitative approach using a goal-oriented evaluation model. Research participants consisted of the principal, Islamic Religious Education teachers, and students involved in the program. Data were collected through interviews, observations, and documentation, and analyzed using the Miles, Huberman, and Saldana model, including data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing. The findings revealed that the TBQ program was implemented systematically through initial ability mapping, regular guidance, and periodic evaluations. The evaluation indicated an improvement in students’ Quran reading skills, reflected by an increase in the proportion of students categorized as good and very good and a decrease in the poor category from 24% to 16%. title: Policy Analysis and Implementation of Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) Programs in Indonesia: A Case Study in Urban and Rural Schools
abstract: This study aims to analyze the policy and implementation of the Free Nutritious Meal Program (MBG) in urban and rural schools in Indonesia, as well as examine stakeholder perceptions and their impact on student participation in the learning process. As a strategic public policy intervention, the MBG program addresses critical micronutrient deficiencies and unequal access to nutritious food, which significantly correlate with cognitive ability, learning concentration, and academic achievement. Utilizing a descriptive qualitative approach, this research collected primary and secondary data through in-depth semi-structured interviews, field observations, and comprehensive documentation studies. The comparative research setting encompasses schools in rural and urban areas to facilitate a holistic analysis of policy implementation dynamics. The findings reveal that although the MBG policy is designed nationally to uniformly improve nutritional status and learning quality, its localized implementation is highly contextual. title: Exploring the Pedagogical Potential of Local Cultural Heritage for Descriptive Writing Instruction: A Case Study of Sedekah Waduk Cengklik in Boyolali Indonesia
abstract: Sedekah Waduk Cengklik are an annual tradition of the Boyolali community which is held as a form of gratitude for the benefits of the existence of the reservoir for the community. This study aims to examine the procession of Sedekah Waduk Cengkliktradition and analyze its potential and integration in learning to write descriptive texts based on local culture. This study uses a qualitative method with a case study approach. The data was analyzed using an interactive analysis model which included data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing and verification. The results of the study show that the procession of Sedekah Waduk Cengklikhas the potential to be integrated into learning to write descriptive texts based on local culture because it has contextual characteristics and presents real objects that can make it easier for students to develop descriptive texts. The integration of these traditions can also be a means of strengthening students' character, including religiosity, creativity, curiosity, love for the homeland, concern for the environment, social concern, and responsibility. title: Implementation of the Generative Model of Quantum Teaching in the Development of Creativity in Writing Lampung Cultural Poetry in PGSD Students
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of the Generative Quantum Teaching learning model in improving poetry writing creativity with Lampung local culture themes for PGSD students. The study used a quantitative approach with an experimental method through a pretest-posttest control group design. The research subjects consisted of an experimental class and a control class of PGSD students at Muhammadiyah Pringsewu University. Data collection techniques used poetry writing tests, observation, and documentation. Data analysis was carried out through descriptive statistics, normality tests, homogeneity tests, and independent sample t-tests. The results showed that the application of the Generative Quantum Teaching model effectively improved students' poetry writing creativity. This was indicated by an increase in the average posttest score of the experimental class of 87.60 compared to the control class of 75.20 with a significance value of 0.002

title: Teaching Religious Moderation through Classical Islamic Texts and Aswaja Studies: A Phenomenological Study at Ma’had Al-Jami’ah Universitas Islam Nusantara Al-Azhaar Lubuklinggau
abstract: This research is motivated by the importance of strengthening religious moderation in Islamic universities in response to a tendency toward religious understanding that is textual, exclusive, and less open to differences. This study aims to analyze the learning of religious moderation through the study of Islamic classics and Aswaja at Ma’had Al-Jami’ah, Nusantara Al-Azhaar Islamic University, Lubuklinggau. The research uses a qualitative approach with a phenomenological design. Data were obtained through observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation, with mudir ma’had, musyrif, teachers, and students as the main sources. The results of the study show that religious moderation learning at Ma’had Al-Jami’ah is carried out through the integration of the study of the materials of the Book of Fathul Qarib, Bidayatul Mujtahid, and Aswaja-an into the hut learning system. This strategy strengthens a balanced understanding of Islam, tolerance, and openness to different sects, and is supported by moral strengthening, language learning, and entrepreneurship development. This research demonstrates that integrating classical books and Aswaja-an values can be an effective pedagogical mode

title: The Historical Development of An Najah Islamic Boarding School in the Advancement of Islamic Education: From Scholarly Tradition to Modern Transformation
abstract: This article examines the historical development of An Najah Islamic Boarding School in Purwokerto as a single-site qualitative case of Islamic educational advancement. It argues that An Najah did not move from tradition to modernity through rupture, but through negotiated continuity: kiai authority, kitab-based learning, devotional discipline, adab, and salaf morality are maintained while modern administration, student services, writing culture, life skills, technology orientation, moderation programs, and institutional partnerships are selectively adopted. Field data were drawn from the An Najah component of a 2023 qualitative research report through interviews, observation, and documentation. The findings show three interrelated patterns. First, An Najah's institutional identity emerged from the founder's experience in student-pesantren education and was formalized through religious study forums, the Kajian Intensif Islam Ramadhan, Ministry of Religious Affairs recognition, and the ethos of being salaf in study, practice, and character while khalaf in service. title: Integrating Qur'anic Values into Islamic Education Tutorial Models: A Case Study of Higher Education Institutions
abstract: This article aims to analyze the integration of Qur'anic values into the tutorial model of Islamic recligious education in higher education, focusing on the reliability of measurement instruments, the correlation between the main constructs, and their practical implications. Data were collected from 68 respondents, the majority of whom were women (95.6%). Reliability tests with Cronbach's Alpha showed strong internal consistency across domains: Qur'anic Integration (α = 0.897), Learning Environment (α = 0.969), Personal Impact (α = 0.969), and Teaching Quality (α = 0.981). Descriptive analysis revealed that Qur'anic Integration obtained the highest average score (M = 4.24), while the Learning Environment obtained the lowest score (M = 3.43). Correlation analysis showed a very strong relationship between Learning Environment and Personal Impact (r = 0.952), Learning Environment and Teaching Quality (r = 0.950), and Personal Impact and Teaching Quality (r = 0.944). These findings suggest that improvements in the learning environment have the potential to have a significant chain effect on personal impact and teaching quality. The study recommends prioritizing structural and pedagogic

title: Bridging Educational Gaps in a Papuan Context: Practicum-Based Learning to Improve Science Achievement and Scientific Attitudes
abstract: This study examined the effect of practicum-based learning on scientific attitudes and cognitive learning outcomes among 60 eighth-grade students in Jayapura, focusing on the human respiratory system, using a quantitative quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design with experimental and control groups. Data were collected through a validated scientific attitude questionnaire and a cognitive learning outcomes test, analyzed using an Independent Samples t-test and a Mann-Whitney U test, respectively. Results showed that practicum-based learning significantly improved students' scientific attitudes (p

title: Research Trends in Arabic Language Learning Based on Contrastive Analysis: A Bibliometric Study in the Scopus Database (2020–2025)
abstract: This study aims to map the development and research trends in Arabic language learning through a contrastive analysis using a bibliometric approach. The data were obtained from the Scopus database for the period 2020–2025 using the keywords "contrastive analysis" and "Arabic learning." The analysis was conducted using VOSviewer to identify publication trends, leading contributors, collaboration patterns, and the conceptual structure of the research field. The results indicate a significant increase in publications since 2023, reflecting growing academic interest in this area. Research contributions are predominantly led by Middle Eastern countries, particularly Saudi Arabia, with a strong pattern of collaborative authorship. Thematically, the studies focus on contrastive analysis and error analysis in comparisons between Arabic and English. In addition, there is an emerging trend toward integrating technologies such as artificial intelligence and deep learning. These findings suggest that the field is evolving toward a more interdisciplinary and data-driven approach. title: Experiential-Based Reflective Learning for Strengthening Metacognitive Ability and Academic Resilience on Students of Tadris Bahasa Indonesia
abstract: This study aims to describe: (1) The Implementation Process of Experiential-Based Reflective Learning in Tadris Bahasa Indonesia Students; (2) The Experiences of Tadris Bahasa Indonesia Students in Strengthening Metacognitive Abilities through Experiential-Based Reflective Learning; and (3) The Experiences of Tadris Bahasa Indonesia Students in Strengthening Academic Resilience through Experiential-Based Reflective Learning. This study utilizes a qualitative phenomenological design grounded in the constructivist-interpretivist paradigm. Data were collected from reflective journals, in-depth interviews, participant observations, and documentation of the experiential-based reflective learning process involving 30 Tadris Bahasa Indonesia students at UIN A.M. Sangadji Ambon, and were subsequently analyzed thematically. The results of this study describe that experiential-based reflective learning for Tadris Bahasa Indonesia students at UIN Ambon is implemented in a cyclical and contextual manner through: (1) The implementation of experiential-based reflective learning takes place cyclically (Concrete Experience -> Reflective Observation -> Abstract Conceptualization -> Active Experimen

title: Strategy and Implementation of Islamic Religious Education in the Era of Digitalization
abstract: The purpose of this study is to explain how Islamic religious education can be implemented with strategies in the digitalization era in schools. The era of digitalization as a result of the increasingly massive development of science and technology that makes changes. Researchers use a qualitative method with a literature study approach or library research, where all data obtained comes from primary and secondary data (books, articles, journals, and other sources). From this research, the results obtained that Islamic Religious Education must be considered for its strategy and implementation in the digitalization of science in the current era where as educators must be literate in the presence of a digital era that is increasingly developing and affecting Islamic religious education and be able to adapt, develop themselves to improve learning, even students get guidance and direction in the use of digital devices. And can apply strategies and methods using digital-based media through existing platforms. This study offers a practical strategic framework and evaluated set of digital platforms that can guide educators and schools in implementing Islamic Religious Education effectively

title: Picture Books Under the Lens: A Bibliometric Mapping of Research Trends
abstract: This study aims to map publication trends, main topics, and research gaps related to picture books in primary schools indexed in Scopus over the past decade. This study answers three main questions: (1) What are the publication trends of research related to picture books in primary schools indexed in Scopus over the past decade? (2) What are the main topics or keywords frequently appearing in research on picture books in primary schools? (3) What research gaps can be identified from the bibliometric analysis of picture books in primary schools? The approach used is bibliometric, with steps including Defining the aim of the research, collecting data on the relevant literature, Analysis and visualization using VOSViewer software, and interpreting the findings and results. The analysis results show that publications related to this topic have increased significantly from 2015 to 2025, with a peak in 2025. Frequently emerging topics in the research include literacy, diversity, language development, and classroom instruction. The study also identified key countries contributing to these publications, such as the United States, the United Kingdom, and China, and noted the important role

title: Da'wah as a Socio-Political Strategy: An Analysis of Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II's Resistance Against Colonialism
abstract: This study investigates Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II’s application of da’wah (Islamic propagation) as a socio-political strategy during his resistance against Dutch colonialism, particularly in his exile to Ternate. It addresses a gap in prior research by focusing on the religious dimension of his leadership, moving beyond his military and diplomatic efforts. The study aims to analyze the role of da’wah in mobilizing social solidarity, promoting religious moderation (wasathiyah), and establishing non-violent resistance. This research uses qualitative historical methods and discourse analysis to examine primary sources, historical documents, and interviews with descendants of Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II. The findings show that Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II utilized da’wah as a tool to strengthen social cohesion through institutions like mosques, pesantren, and the Sammaniyah Order. His moderate approach, emphasizing tolerance, justice, and cultural accommodation, united diverse societal groups and preserved their cultural-religious identity under colonial oppression. This study concludes that da’wah was a powerful strategy for integrating faith with social and political objectives. It

title: Development of a Meaningful Learning Model Based on Fishermen's Environment to Form Students' Creative Behavior
abstract: The purpose of this research is to develop of a meaningful learning model based on fishermen’s environment to form students' creative behavior. This research is designed based on ADDIE development model. The population in this study were all junior high school students in coastal Cirebon. Data collection techniques used in this study include observation, interview, and lift distribution. Researchers will process and analyze the data using descriptive statistical analysis. Data analysis was carried out in three stages during this study, namely data analysis during preliminary studies (empirical studies and literature studies), then data analysis during the design model development process, and finally, data analysis as a process of producing model effectiveness test results. Based on the results of this study, a meaningful learning model based on the fishing environment can increase the creativity of Cirebon coastal junior high school students. This model connects new knowledge with what students already know, making the material easier to understand and encouraging creativity.

title: Value in Ngabésan at Rengasdengklok Subdistrict, Karawang Regency as the Basis for Character Education Development in Elementary School
abstract: Ngabésan is one of the traditional Sundanese wedding ceremonies that symbolizes family unity and support prior to marriage. In this procession, the groom's family and relatives visit the bride's family, bringing symbolic gifts that represent respect, commitment, and the beginning of a new familial relationship. Beyond its ceremonial function, ngabésan embodies cultural values that have significant educational potential, particularly as a resource for cultural literacy in elementary education. This study aims to identify the educational values embedded in the ngabésan tradition and explore their relevance to character and cultural literacy education in elementary schools. The research employed a qualitative approach using literature review and field study methods. Data were collected through interviews and direct observation and analyzed using semiotic theory to interpret the meanings of the symbols and practices within the tradition. The findings reveal five core values embedded in the ngabésan ceremony: mutual cooperation, responsibility, togetherness, harmony, and mutual assistance. These values are closely aligned with the objectives of character education and can be effectively

title: Determinats of Deep Learning Oriented Teaching Behavior: A Theory of Planned Behavior Perpective among Special Education Teachers
abstract: This study addresses the growing demand for deep learning-oriented instruction in 21st-century education, particularly in special education, where instructional practices involve high levels of complexity. The study aims to analyze the determinants of deep learning oriented teaching behavior among special education teachers using the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). A quantitative explanatory survey design was employed, involving 66 teachers selected through snowball sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed through hierarchical multiple regression. The results indicate that perceived behavioral control (PBC) and subjective norm (SN) significantly predict both intention and teaching behavior, while attitude toward behavior (ATB) does not show a significant effect when controlling for other variables. Intention significantly predicts behavior; however, its additional contribution is relatively small (ΔR² = 0.013), indicating that behavioral implementation is influenced not only by intention but also by professional competence and environmental factors. title: Mapping the Paradigm Shift in Teachers’ Roles: A Bibliometric and Survey-Based Analysis in 21st-Century Education
abstract: Rapid social and digital transformations have fundamentally reshaped education systems, leading to a redefinition of teachers’ roles in the 21st century that extends beyond technological integration to encompass epistemological, pedagogical, and structural changes. This study aims to analyze the conceptual structure, intellectual evolution, and global collaboration patterns of the paradigm shift in teachers’ roles, while also examining its empirical manifestation in practice. A mixed-method approach with an integrative design was employed, combining a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) based on the PRISMA 2020 protocol, bibliometric analysis, and a quantitative survey. Data were retrieved from the Scopus database (2016–2026), resulting in 85 peer-reviewed articles following a rigorous selection process, and complemented by survey responses from 80 teachers across Indonesia. Bibliometric mapping using VOSviewer reveals that the emerging paradigm is structured across three interrelated dimensions: pedagogical, technological, and structural. title: Development of a Pocket Book of Everyday English Expressions for Use in Dormitories in the Context of Islamic Boarding Schools
abstract: This study aims to develop a Pocket Book of Daily English Expressions for boarding school students in the pesantren context to improve students’ speaking skills in everyday communication. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) method using the ADDIE model, consisting of analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation stages. The participants involved students from grades 7, 8, and 9 in an Islamic boarding school in Cimahi, West Java, Indonesia. Peer facilitators from grades 8 and 9 were trained to assist the implementation process. Data were collected through classroom observation, progress evaluation, post-tests, and student feedback. The findings showed significant improvement in students’ speaking performance after four weeks of implementation. Speaking participation increased from 45% to 89%, vocabulary mastery improved from 40% to 86%, and students’ confidence in speaking English rose from 38% to 85%. The contextual materials provided in the pocket book helped students practice English expressions related to dormitory life, making learning more meaningful and practical. In addition, the peer-facilitator approach created a collaborative learning envir

title: Relational Leadership Matters: Leader–Member Exchange, Managerial Skills, and Teacher Performance in Madrasah Ibtidaiyah
abstract: The inconsistent contribution of leadership practices to teacher performance indicates the need to examine relational and managerial leadership within the specific context of Islamic elementary education. This study aimed to analyze the partial and simultaneous contributions of Leader–Member Exchange and madrasah principals’ managerial skills to the performance of Madrasah Ibtidaiyah teachers. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 195 teachers proportionally selected from a population of 448 teachers across 38 public and private Madrasah Ibtidaiyah in Way Kanan Regency, Lampung Province, Indonesia. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and analyzed through multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics version 20. The results showed that Leader–Member Exchange made a positive and significant partial contribution to teacher performance (B = 0.684; t = 2.236; p = 0.027), whereas madrasah principals’ managerial skills did not make a significant direct contribution (B = −0.525; t = −0.340; p = 0.734). title: The Development of Islamic Religious Education Curriculum based on Independent Learning and Independent Campus in Higher Education
abstract: The development of an Islamic Religious Education (PAI) curriculum based on Freedom to Learn and Independent Campus (MBKM) in higher education is a strategic effort to address the demands of changing times, the need for 21st-century competencies, and the dynamics of religious life in the digital era. The PAI curriculum, integrated with the MBKM policy, provides students with the opportunity to learn more flexibly, independently, and contextually through project-based learning, internships, teaching assistantships, research, and student exchanges. This study aims to analyze the concept, implementation, and challenges of developing an MBKM-based PAI curriculum in higher education. Using a qualitative approach with R&D and the Rowntree model, this study illustrates how the PAI curriculum is designed to focus not only on mastering religious material but also on strengthening soft skills, digital literacy, and critical thinking skills and developing moderate character. The study results indicate that the implementation of an MBKM-based PAI curriculum can increase the relevance of learning to real-world needs, broaden students' learning experiences, and strengthen the pedagogical and pro

title: Comparative Study of Team Games Tournament, Numbered Heads Together, and STAD Learning Models on Students’ Learning Outcomes in Terms of Gender
abstract: This study aims to determine the comparative effectiveness of the Team Games Tournament (TGT), Numbered Heads Together (NHT), and Student Teams Achievement Division (STAD) learning models on Islamic Education learning outcomes among sixth-grade students at SDN Permata Hijau Rancaekek, with gender as a controlling variable. This study employs a quantitative approach using a comparative method. Data were obtained from students’ learning outcomes and analyzed using SPSS 26. Data analysis was conducted using a two-way ANOVA test and non-parametric tests because the data were not normally distributed. title: Transformative Spiritual Model: Integration of Holistic Education-Based Deep Learning in Strengthening Students' Islamic Character in Primary Schools
abstract: This study examines the implementation of deep learning within a holistic education framework to strengthen Islamic character through a transformative spiritual model in elementary education. The research analyzes the integration of Intellectual Quotient (IQ) and Spiritual Quotient (SQ) grounded in mindful, meaningful, and joyful learning. Employing a qualitative, holistic single-case study at SD Muhammadiyah Bantul Kota, Yogyakarta, data were gathered through participatory observations, documentation analysis, and in-depth interviews with the principal, teachers, and sixth-grade students. Data were analyzed using an interactive model involving condensation, display, and source triangulation. The findings reveal that deep learning effectively integrates cognitive and spiritual dimensions; for instance, science lessons transcend conceptual understanding by incorporating spiritual reflections on divine greatness. The three foundations of deep learning foster intrinsic religiosity, transforming practices such as prayer and dhikr into internal spiritual needs rather than mere formal obligations. Furthermore, the study identifies the emergence of a transformative spiritual culture evide

title: Design and Implementation of Moodle-Based Online Summative Assessment in Islamic Religious Education at Primary Schools
abstract: Manual summative assessment is no longer relevant to the transformation of Islamic education in digital learning. Therefore, an easy, efficient assessment system is needed to support digital learning. The purpose of this study is to design an online summative assessment using Moodle, assisted by Android, to create an effective and efficient assessment. The research method used in this study is a mixed-method sequential explanatory design. A qualitative approach is used to design an online summative Moodle application with a digital literature study review. Meanwhile, a quantitative approach was used to test the effectiveness of the online summative model design in primary schools, with 10 learners from classes 4, 5, and 6. The data from the literature review were presented inductively to present the steps of the Android-assisted Moodle application in conducting online summative assessments. The data on the application of Moodle in summative assessment were analysed using a t-test in SPSS 20 to determine the effectiveness of Android-assisted Moodle in creating assessments that are both effective and efficient. title: Transformational Leadership and the Eco-Organizational Culture: Driving Educational Quality in Adiwiyata Schools
abstract: This study addresses the critical gap between successful environmental programs and low instructional leadership scores by investigating a paradoxical phenomenon at an Adiwiyata school. The primary objective is to thoroughly analyze the role of the principal's transformational leadership in building a sustainable quality education culture. Utilizing a qualitative case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews, participatory observation, and comprehensive documentation. The results reveal that the principal successfully applies four transformational dimensions: idealized influence through authentic eco-friendly behavior, inspirational motivation by cultivating collective enthusiasm, intellectual stimulation by fostering dynamic environment-based learning innovations, and individualized consideration through empowering supervision and personalized support. In conclusion, the principal's transformational leadership synergistically establishes a robust quality education culture. title: Organizing Islamic Tarbiyah to Create Superior Character in the Era of Society 5.0 for Students
abstract: This research seeks to examine the implementation of Islamic education (tarbiyah Islamiyah) in fostering excellent student character within the context of the Society 5.0 era at MTs Al-Wahdah Kendari. A qualitative naturalistic methodology was employed, utilizing non-participant observation, in-depth interviews, and document analysis as data collection methods. The results show that the organization is integrated in four areas: (1) human resources are organized hierarchically through the foundation-madrasah structure, role division, and committee involvement as accountability partners; (2) academic activities are managed through learning outcome-based intracurricular activities, active learning models, and cross-subject P5R projects guided by mapping the dimensions-elements-subelements of student profiles; (3) non-academic activities are organized through mandatory and elective extracurricular activities with schedules, mentors, and development targets aligned with P2R values; and (4) madrasah culture is built through a functional work team that manages integrated religious-social habits within the academic calendar. title: The Contestation of Differentiation of Educator Capabilities on Learning Effectiveness in the Digital Era
abstract: This study aims to explore the relationship between educator skill differentiation and learning effectiveness in the digital era. A quantitative approach was used to analyze the influence of variables such as lecturer age, length of teaching, technology mastery, experience and depth of material, as well as relationships with students and pedagogical approaches on learning effectiveness. The results of the regression analysis showed that experience and depth of material had the most significant influence on learning effectiveness, with a regression coefficient of 1.679 (t = 4.233, p = 0.001). Furthermore, technology mastery showed a positive effect approaching significance (coefficient = 0.1336, t = 1.966, p = 0.067), indicating the importance of technology integration in learning. However, variables such as lecturer age and length of teaching did not have a significant influence. The F-test yielded an F-statistic of 159.70 with a p-value of 4.57, confirming that the combination of variables in this model has a significant influence on learning effectiveness. title: The Effectiveness of the Literature Circle Method in Improving the Bahasa Rumi Writing Skills of Mattayom 3 Students at Ban Kalisa School
abstract: This study was motivated by the low level of Bahasa Rumi writing skills among Mattayom 3 students at Ban Kalisa School, who grow up in a linguistic environment where Thai, Malay Jawi, and Bahasa Rumi intersect. This study aims to describe the students’ initial and final abilities, as well as to analyze the effectiveness of the Literature Circle method in improving Bahasa Rumi writing skills. The study employed a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design. The research sample consisted of 27 students in the experimental class and 25 students in the control class. The data were obtained through Bahasa Rumi writing tests administered before and after the treatment, then analyzed using descriptive statistics and hypothesis testing. The results showed that the mean pre-test score of the experimental class was 62.19, while that of the control class was 61.40. After the treatment, the mean post-test score of the experimental class increased to 76.93, whereas that of the control class became 68.40. The gain score of the experimental class reached 14.74, which was higher than that of the control class at 7.00. Hypothesis testing indicated significa

title: Integration of Problem-Based Teaching Factory (PBTF) Method with Learning Management System: A SmartPLS Analysis of Student Learning Outcomes and Engagement
abstract: Digital transformation through Learning Management Systems (LMS) has expanded access to learning in higher education, but its effectiveness is highly dependent on student engagement. In vocational education, the challenges are increasingly complex because learning must integrate cognitive, affective, and psychomotor competencies relevant to industry standards. The integration of Problem-Based Learning and Teaching Factory within the LMS-based Problem-Based Teaching Factory (PBTF-LMS) framework offers a holistic approach, but the mediating mechanism of competency on student engagement has not been widely tested structurally. This study aims to analyze the effect of PBTF-LMS implementation on student engagement through the mediating role of mastery of tri-domain competencies (cognitive, affective, psychomotor) in Automotive Education students. This study uses a predictive quantitative design with a Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) approach. The sample consisted of 30 students selected purposively. Data were collected through a Likert questionnaire and LMS activity logs, then analyzed using SmartPLS 4 with outer and inner model evaluation and bootstrapping

title: Optimizing Microlearning in English Language Learning: The Role of Learning Involvement and Independence on Vocational School Student Satisfaction
abstract: This study presents the optimization of microlearning in English learning for vocational high school students by emphasizing the role of learning engagement and independence on satisfaction and language skills. The background of the study stems from the low achievement of vocational high school students' English skills and the need for learning strategies that are more adaptive to the characteristics of the digital generation. The purpose of this study is to analyze the influence of microlearning content, learning engagement, and learning independence on English skills and student learning satisfaction, both directly and in complex structural relationships. The method used is a quantitative approach with an explanatory research design through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) analysis of 300 grade X students of a state vocational high school in Mojokerto. Data were collected through a Likert scale questionnaire and an English proficiency test, then analyzed to test validity, reliability, and the relationship between variables in the structural model. The results showed that learning engagement was the most dominant factor that significantly influenced Eng

title: Enhancing Memorize the Qur'an through Qur'ans Aplications and Different Students' Critical Thinking Levels
abstract: The memorization of the Qur'an (ḥifẓ al-Qur'ān) has been a central aspect of Islamic education for centuries. The purpose of this study is to analyze the differences in memorizing the Quran using digital and murrotal Qurans, critical thinking of students at different levels and the influence of interaction between memorizing the Quran using digital and murrotal Qurans on memorizing the Quran. Quantitative methodology was implemented in the present research, using a quasi-experimental design. This design integrates a non-equivalent control group methodology with a two-way factorial design (2 x 3 ANOVA). This investigation employed a sample of 300 students. A total of 150 participants comprised each cohort. The participants of this investigation were first-year pupils at Sultan Ageng Tirtayasa University in Banten. This research yielded three principal findings: 1) A disparity exists in the memorisation capabilities of students utilising digital Qur'an against auditory murrotal. 2) There exists a disparity in the capacity to memorise the Qur'an among pupils with high, medium, and low levels of critical thinking. 3) An interaction exists between the utilisation of digital Qur'an and a

title: The Construction of Conceptual Metaphors in the Discourse of BIPA Learners: A Cross-Cultural Thematic Study
abstract: Metaphorical competence has been recognized as essential to advanced communicative proficiency in a second language, yet Indonesian as a Foreign Language (BIPA) has remained entirely absent from this research landscape, despite rapid global growth in learner numbers across typologically diverse language backgrounds. This study synthesizes internationally recognized empirical studies published between 2010 and 2025 on how second-language learners construct and use conceptual metaphor in discourse, with direct implications for BIPA instruction. Analysis was conducted using a Cross-Cultural Cognitive Discourse Analysis framework integrating Conceptual Metaphor Theory, Critical Metaphor Analysis, and van Dijk's sociocognitive approach, with metaphor identification following the MIPVU procedure. Three dominant patterns were identified. First, learners systematically transfer conceptual schemas from their first language into Indonesian discourse, producing utterances that are grammatically correct but culturally incongruent conceptual fluency failure with the extent and type of transfer varying predictably by language family. title: The Effectiveness of Context-Based Experimental Learning in Enhancing Elementary Students’ Problem-Solving Skills on Changes in the States of Matter
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of context-based experimental learning in improving elementary students’ problem-solving skills on the topic of changes in the states of matter. Addressing the persistent gap in Indonesian students’ scientific problem-solving performance reported by PISA 2022, the research employed a one-group pretest–posttest quasi-experimental design involving 18 fourth-grade students from MI Ma’arif NU Cipete. Students’ problem-solving ability defined as the capacity to understand problems, devise strategies, and evaluate solutions was assessed using essay-based tests. The results showed a substantial improvement, with an N-Gain score of 0.72 (high category), indicating strong learning effectiveness. These findings demonstrate that context-based experimental learning not only strengthens conceptual understanding but also fosters active engagement and higher-order thinking skills (HOTS). The study provides empirical evidence supporting this method as a viable instructional strategy in elementary science education. Future research should extend the model to broader topics and diverse school contexts to confirm its generalizability.

title: Early Childhood Digital Literacy Strategies and Approaches: A Systematic Review PRISMA with Watase Uake Web Use
abstract: The incorporation of digital media into early literacy learning is the main emphasis of this research, which examines digital literacy methods and techniques for improving children's early reading abilities. The study examined Scopus-indexed papers released between 2015 and 2025, utilizing a methodical literature review based on the PRISMA 2020 framework, and used the Watase Uwake tool to evaluate the use of digital literacy in early childhood education. Eight of the 133 identified articles satisfied the inclusion criteria for comprehensive analysis. According to the results, interactive digital media like augmented reality, digital storytelling, and instructional apps greatly aids in the early childhood development of reading comprehension, vocabulary, and phonological awareness. But the success of these digital interventions depends heavily on teachers' willingness to incorporate technology into the curriculum and on parents' active role in directing their children's digital experiences. In particular, there are research gaps pertaining to the roles of parental support and teacher readiness, particularly in the Indonesian setting. This study offers fresh perspectives on the integ

title: The Dynamics of Implementing Religious Development Programs in Secondary Schools in the Digital Era
abstract: This study aims to analyze the dynamics of the implementation of religious guidance programs in secondary schools in the digital era. The study used a descriptive qualitative approach with a case study type conducted in three types of schools: SMA, SMK, and MAN. Data collection techniques were carried out through observation, interviews, and documentation, involving principals, teachers, and students involved in religious activities. The results of the study indicate that the religious guidance program is implemented in a structured and sustainable manner through daily, weekly, and annual activities, such as Quranic recitation, congregational prayers, religious lectures, infaq activities, and commemorations of Islamic holidays. Each type of school has different characteristics, with SMA and SMK tending to emphasize the habituation of religious activities, while MAN shows a stronger integration between learning and worship practices. However, program implementation faces various dynamics in the digital era, such as the use of devices that disrupt concentration, limited teacher supervision, a lack of activity variety, and the influence of the social environment. title: Strengthening Local Wisdom through Extracurricular Activities: Integrated Islamic Education in Banda Aceh
abstract: The development of Integrated Islamic Elementary Schools (SDIT) in Banda Aceh reflects the diverse dynamics of efforts to integrate national education, Islamic values, and local wisdom in Aceh. However, studies specifically examining the process of strengthening local wisdom through extracurricular activities in integrated Islamic education remain limited. This study aims to deeply examine the transformation of strengthening Acehnese local wisdom through extracurricular activities and reveal the characteristics and advantages of implementing integrated Islamic education in SDITs in Banda Aceh. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach using a case study method at three Integrated Islamic Elementary Schools (SDIT); SD Islam Al-Azhar Cairo Banda Aceh, SDIT Nurul Ishlah Banda Aceh, and SDIT Quantum School Aceh. Data were collected through observation, semi-structured interviews, and document analysis, and were then analyzed using the Miles and Huberman model with triangulation techniques to ensure validity. The results of the study demonstrate that extracurricular activities play a pivotal role in reinforcing and enhancing the values of Aceh's Islamic-based local wisdom. T

title: Deep Learning from a Qur’anic Perspective: An Analysis of Mindful, Meaningful, and Joyful Learning in Arabic Language Education
abstract: Arabic language learning continues to face challenges related to surface-level instructional practices that emphasize memorization and structural mastery, often failing to foster learners’ awareness, meaning-making, and meaningful learning experiences. In response to shallow learning, the concept of deep learning has emerged in contemporary educational discourse; however, it has largely been developed within Western cognitive frameworks that tend to overlook the spiritual dimension of human learning. This article aims to analyze the concept of deep learning from a Qur’anic perspective through the framework of Mindful, Meaningful, and Joyful Learning and to examine its implications for Arabic language education. This study adopts a qualitative approach with a library research design. The data sources include selected Qur’anic verses related to learning, classical and contemporary Qur’anic exegesis, and relevant educational literature. Data were analyzed using a thematic–interpretative approach. title: Development of Interdisciplinary-Based Islamic Religious Education Teaching Materials in State Universities
abstract: This research aims to develop interdisciplinary Islamic Religious Education (PAI) teaching materials tailored to the needs of students at public universities (PTU). The interdisciplinary approach is used in response to the dichotomy between religious studies and general studies that is still prevalent in the higher education system. By integrating Islamic values into various disciplines such as science, technology, economics, and social studies, PAI teaching materials can provide students with a more contextual and applicable understanding. The research method used is Research and Development (R&D) with qualitative and quantitative approaches, involving needs analysis, teaching materials design, expert validation, and limited student trials. The results indicate that interdisciplinary PAI teaching materials can increase student engagement, strengthen the relevance of PAI in the context of modern science, and shape critical and adaptive religious character. These findings suggest that integrating Islamic values into PAI teaching materials can be an effective strategy in building higher education that is not only intellectually superior, but also morally and personally developed. title: Strengthening the Buddy Program is an Effort to Prevent Acts of Violence in the School Environment
abstract: Violence in schools, whether physical, verbal, psychological, or social, remains a serious problem that threatens a safe and character-building educational climate. Bullying, intimidation, and social exclusion not only impact students' academic achievement but also impact their mental health, self-confidence, and personality development. One approach considered effective and contextual in preventing violence in schools is the implementation of the Buddy Program, a peer mentoring program that systematically connects students in supportive, egalitarian, and socially conscious relationships. The purpose of this study was to analyze the strengthening of the Buddy Program as a preventive strategy to suppress and prevent acts of violence in schools. This research used a qualitative approach with a case study design, focusing on educational units that have implemented the Buddy Program as part of their character-building and violence prevention policies. The results showed that strengthening the Buddy Program was able to build more positive social relationships among students, increase empathy, and strengthen social support networks within the school environment. title: Transforming Student Learning: The Role of Digital Library Utilization and the Quality of Digital Collections on Performance and Learning Outcomes with Information Literacy Moderation
abstract: The transformation of learning in higher education places digital libraries beyond simply providing information access, but rather as strategic instruments that determine the quality of student performance and learning outcomes. This study aims to comprehensively examine the influence of digital library use and the quality of digital collections on student performance and learning outcomes, with information literacy as a moderating variable. The study used a quantitative approach with an explanatory design using the Structural Equation Modeling method on 200 students of the Graduate School of PGRI Adi Buana University Surabaya, intakes of 2023 to 2025. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using measurement and structural models to test the direct and indirect effects between variables. The results showed that the quality of digital collections significantly influenced student learning outcomes and information literacy, while the use of digital libraries had no direct effect on student performance. title: Negotiating Identity through Code-Switching: English and Buginese Language in Academic and Social Discourse
abstract: This study examines at the sociolinguistic phenomena of code-switching among English-Buginese bilingual university students, with a focus on how it helps them negotiate their identities in academic and social settings. Using a qualitative case study approach, data were collected from simulated but contextually authentic interactions such as classroom discussions, peer conversations, and semi-structured interviews. Based on Gumperz's (1982) interactional sociolinguistics and Myers-Scotton's (1993) markedness model, the analysis identified three types of code-switching: inter-sentential, intra-sentential, and tag-switching. The findings show that in academic settings, English is frequently employed to communicate formality, academic authority, and alignment with global academic discourse, whereas Buginese is utilized to maintain solidarity, cultural identity, and shared heritage. In social situations, code-switching promotes humor, emotional expression, and pragmatic efficiency. Switching can be triggered by topic switches, lexical gaps, emphasis, or audience adjustment.
